title: Newborn umbilical cord care
what: After the hospital, your baby has a piece of umbilical cord left. It dries and falls off on its own, and the spot heals. Your job is to keep it clean and dry.
why: For all newborns in the first weeks of life.
duration: the stump usually falls off in 1 to 3 weeks, and the spot heals in a few more days
tell_doctor: If the skin around the navel turns red, swells or smells bad
If fluid or blood oozes from the spot
If the stump has not fallen off after 3 weeks
If your baby has a fever or is limp

prepare.title: Cleanliness
prepare.text: Wash your hands before caring for the navel.

prepare.title: Dryness
prepare.text: Usually dry care is advised now: keep the navel clean and open to the air. Ask your pediatrician whether any treatment is needed.

prepare.title: Diaper
prepare.text: Fold the top of the diaper below the navel so it does not rub or get wet.

prepare.title: Bathing
prepare.text: Your pediatrician will say whether you can bathe your baby in a tub.

steps: Look at the navel and the skin around it
If the spot got dirty, rinse it with boiled water and pat dry
Leave the navel open to the air for a few minutes
Put on a diaper, folding the top below the navel
Do not pull on the stump, even if it is almost off
feel: It does not hurt your baby. The cord has no nerves
A drop of blood when the stump falls off is possible and passes
after: After the stump falls off, keep the spot clean for a few more days
Do not cover the navel with plasters or dressings
Show the navel to your pediatrician at the home visit
red_flags: Redness around the navel is spreading, swelling, pus or smell: see the pediatrician urgently
Your baby has a fever, is limp or feeds poorly: call your local emergency number
Bleeding from the navel does not stop

faq.q: Do I need to put antiseptic dye on the navel?
faq.a: Usually not now. It is enough to keep it clean and dry. Check with your pediatrician.

faq.q: The navel bulges when my baby cries. Is that dangerous?
faq.a: Often it is an umbilical hernia, which is common in babies. Show it to the pediatrician, who will say what to do.

reminders.text: Show your baby's navel to the pediatrician at the next check. Keep the spot clean and dry.
